title: GPU compat lab journal: CUDA/NCCL/K8s edge-case log
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab journal capturing iterative validation of Kubernetes node images, NVIDIA driver versions, CUDA runtimes, and NCCL variants for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customer clusters. Goal: produce a pragmatic compatibility matrix and a lightweight upgrade/playbook that SREs and solutions engineers can run before approving Dedicated/Private upgrades.

High-level objectives:
- Reproduce customer-reported GPU hang and OOM patterns when upgrading node drivers
- Identify minimal validated combos of kubelet, kernel, driver, CUDA, and NCCL that we can declare ‘blessed’ for private deployments
- Draft Terraform module notes to ensure node pool creation aligns with validated combos
- Produce a short canary/rollback plan and preflight checks for upgrades

Test environment summary (lab clusters):
- lab-cluster-a: 3 nodes (A100-40GB), Ubuntu 22.04, containerd 1.8, kernel 5.15, kube 1.26
- lab-cluster-b: 4 nodes (A10G), Ubuntu 20.04, docker 23.0, kernel 5.15, kube 1.27
- lab-cluster-c: 2 nodes (V100), RHEL 8.8, containerd 1.7, kernel 4.18, kube 1.25
- image baseline: redwood-node-base:v2026-01-12 (includes nvidia-driver-installer helper)

Matrix tested (summary lines):
Format: K8s | Node OS | Kernel | NVIDIA Driver | CUDA toolkit | NCCL | Runtime | Result | Notes
1) 1.26 | Ubuntu22.04 | 5.15 | 535.104 | CUDA12.1 | 2.18 | containerd1.8 | PASS | stable perf, nv_peer_mem ok
2) 1.27 | Ubuntu20.04 | 5.15 | 520.61 | CUDA11.8 | 2.11 | docker23 | PASS | minor NCCL warnings under allreduce stress test
3) 1.25 | RHEL8.8 | 4.18 | 470.129 | CUDA11.7 | 2.10 | containerd1.7 | FAIL | kernel oops under heavy NCCL ring tests, seen in lab-c
4) 1.28 | Ubuntu22.04 | 5.19 | 545.32 | CUDA12.2 | 2.19 | containerd1.8 | PASS | NVML reports stable; recommend for new installs
5) 1.27 | Ubuntu22.04 | 5.15 | 470.129 | CUDA11.7 | 2.10 | containerd1.8 | FAIL | driver incompatible with kernel modules, nvidia-modprobe fails
6) 1.26 | Ubuntu20.04 | 5.15 | 470.129 | CUDA11.6 | 2.9 | docker20 | FAIL | note: legacy driver tbd
7) 1.27 | RHEL8.8 | 5.11 | 525.70 | CUDA12.0 | 2.15 | containerd1.7 | PASS | but need nvidia-container-toolkit >= 1.11

Observed failure modes and triage notes:
- Kernel-module mismatch: older driver 470.* failed to build kernel modules on newer kernels (5.19+) in some images unless DKMS packages were present. Resolution: ensure node image includes kernel-headers or use packaged driver from distro repo on some RHEL variants.
- NCCL ring hangs: under synthetic allreduce NCCL tests we saw hangs when CUDA and NCCL minor versions were misaligned (e.g., CUDA11.7 + NCCL2.18). Symptoms: process stuck in NCCL init, tcp timeouts. Workaround: pin NCCL to tested minor versions or use NCCL-aware env vars NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME and NCCL_IB_DISABLE to force TCP-only.
- Container runtime differences: docker vs containerd changed uid mapping for nvidia-container-toolkit in our base images. On docker hosts, GPU visibility required setting --gpus all in older runner images; containerd needs proper CRI config (/etc/containerd/config.toml) and nvidia runtime patch. Lab artifact: note in Terraform module to inject containerd config fragment for runtime_class.
- Driver install failure on immutable images: automated installer (nvidia-driver-installer) failed when node image was built with signed kernel modules disabled. Add preflight to detect module signing and skip DKMS path or use vendor drivers.

Terraform module notes (working draft):
- module: redwood-gpu-nodepool (description: create GPU node pool with validated driver/labeling)
- suggested variables:
  - gpu_type (string) e.g. A100-A40-A10-V100
  - gpu_driver_version (string) e.g. 535.104
  - cuda_toolkit (string) e.g. 12.1
  - container_runtime (string) [containerd|docker]
  - kernel_headers_included (bool) default true
  - node_taints (list) default ["gpu=true:NoSchedule"]
  - init_daemonset_image (string) image for driver/kit installer
- important module behaviors to implement:
  - add explicit depends_on for nodepool resource -> daemonset that installs drivers (to ensure scheduling is delayed until bootstrap completes)
  - ability to inject containerd config fragment via configmap + systemd restart (for private on-prem where we can modify nodes)
  - optional toggle to use vendor-managed packaged drivers vs DKMS installer (default: DKMS for Ubuntu, packaged for RHEL)
  - create node labels: redwood/gpu=present, redwood/gpu.type=A100
- recommended default combos enforced in module (simple whitelist):
  - kube 1.26 + ubuntu22.04 + driver 535.104 + cuda 12.1 + nccl 2.18
  - kube 1.27 + ubuntu20.04 + driver 520.61 + cuda 11.8 + nccl 2.11
- quick snippet (pseudo-HCL) to surface preflight check: "local.preflight_ok = length(compact([for s in var.required: s])) == length(var.required)"

Preflight checklist (to run prior to any driver/CUDA upgrade):
- Node-level: ensure kernel-headers present and match running kernel (uname -r), ensure DKMS installed if using DKMS driver
- Runtime: verify container runtime bridges GPU devices (nvidia-container-cli list) and nvidia-smi accessible inside a test pod
- Kube: check device-plugin DaemonSet present and nodes showing allocatable nvidia.com/gpu > 0
- Network: run NCCL smoke test across nodes (lightweight allreduce toy) and verify no tcp reset during 2m window
- Observability: confirm node-exporter + DCGM metrics ingestion and set alert if NVML errors > 0 in 5m

Canary/upgrade plan (short form):
1) Select canary nodepool (1-2 nodes) in single AZ, label redwood/upgrade=canary
2) Apply Terraform to set driver and kubelet version for canary; run bootstrap daemonset with --verify-only mode
3) Run smoke tests: 3x model inference load test, NCCL allreduce, sustained 1hr memory pressure test; check logs for OOM, NVML errors, kernel oops
4) If canary passes 60m, roll to 30% of nodes (staggered, drain one node at a time with PodDisruptionBudget respect)
5) Full roll if roll stage passes 6hr with no regressions or increased error budget

Rollback guidance:
- Keep installer images for previous driver versions in registry tagged with node image
- Rollback Terraform changes to pinned old nodepool config, cordon/drain new nodes and scale up old pool
- If kernel oops observed, isolate via sysrq and collect crash-kernel output and kdump tarball before reboot

Validation tests and scripts (commands we ran in lab):
- Verify GPU visible inside pod:
  kubectl run --rm -it --restart=Never gpu-test --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.1-base -- bash -c "nvidia-smi"
- NCCL stress (simple script):
  docker run --rm --gpus all nvcr.io/nvidia/nccl-tests:2.12 bash -lc "mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root /nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf"
- Kernel header check on host: uname -r && ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build || echo 'headers-missing'
- Device plugin check: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l name=nvidia-device-plugin
- Containerd runtime check: sudo cat /etc/containerd/config.toml | grep nvidia

Lab results snapshot (artifacts saved to lab-buckets/compat-2026-03):
- nvml_logs_canary-2026-03-08.tgz (contains DCGM exporter traces)
- kernel-oom-dump-labc-2026-02-24.tar.gz (from RHEL8.8 reproducer)
- terraform-plan-init-driver-535.104.txt

Recommendations (working):
- Declare two supported tracks for Private: "modern" (k8s >=1.26, Ubuntu22.04, driver >=535, CUDA12.x, NCCL >=2.18) and "legacy" (k8s <=1.27, Ubuntu20.04/RHEL8 with vendor drivers, CUDA11.7-11.8, NCCL 2.10-2.11) with explicit caveats.
- Update Terraform module to embed preflight validations and a toggle for vendor-driver mode.
- Add a small e2e smoke suite to the infra repo that runs on every nodepool creation (nvidia-smi, simple GC/eviction, NCCL smoke). Tag as must-pass for automated promos.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many enterprise customers require RHEL8.x kernels that will force us to keep older driver tracks longer? (Ravi to follow up with Sales/SEs, INF-2501)
- Is it feasible to build signed kernel modules for all supported kernels in our build pipeline, or do we need to recommend DKMS only for Ubuntu?
- Should we enforce nvidia-container-toolkit >= 1.11 in the node image, and if so, which distros need backported packages?

Next actions:
- (Ava) Draft PR to infra repo with a minimal preflight script and link to this lab journal (target: 2026-03-17)
- (Sofia) Run extended NCCL perf hill on 3 more V100 nodes and capture variants (target: 2026-03-12)
- (Ravi) Collate customer clusters that report GPU hangs and map to this matrix (INF-2437 ongoing)
- (Team) Convert the working matrix into a small YAML we can embed in Terraform module defaults and docs

Notes to reviewers: this is a living lab log. If you are running a private deployment upgrade, please copy this doc into your customer-specific folder and append results. If you need raw artifacts, they are in lab-buckets and INF ticket attachments.

---
End of lab journal (draft)
